speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're dealing with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand what's causing these symptoms, can you tell me how long you've had the fever and if the skin lesions are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That self-resolving knee pain and your recent camping trip in Minnesota are very concerning; did you have any tick bites, and do you recall seeing a rash? Have you had any joint pain in other joints besides your knee?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (Left Wrist)
Based on the history of a self-resolving knee pain, recent camping in Minnesota, and the classic presentation of painful wrist arthritis with violaceous lesions, do you recall any specific tick bites during your trip, and have you been treated with antibiotics for the knee yet?
